subject: MAP: Benchmark reporting kit and close checklist
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@skyline.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Benchmark reporting kit and close checklist

Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, Skyline's MAP is trending toward an end-of-quarter decision and you asked for a compact set of performance evidence we can share with your engineering and procurement teams. I put together a concise reporting kit that aligns to the MAP milestones and the evaluation plan you shared.

What I'm sending now (attached):
- benchmark_raw.csv — full CSV export of the load tests (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, TTFT, concurrency traces)
- map_reporting_kit_slide_deck.pdf — 6-slide summary for your execs (TL;DR + key metrics + risk/fallback plan)
- exec_readout_onepager.pdf — one-page readout PM/VP level
- dashboard_snapshot.png — snapshot of the live dashboard showing the 95th percentile latency curve during the peak run

Quick notes on the data:
- Test harness: Redwood reference runner v2.1, seq_len 512, 1500 concurrent connections for concurrency test; synthetic and production-like prompt sets included (see CSV meta rows)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) measured end-to-end from request arrival to first token sent back; we included cold-starts and warmed pools in separate columns
- Throughput measured as tokens/sec and requests/sec across multiple instance classes (g4dn-equivalent and A100-equivalent rows included)

Next steps I propose for the MAP:
1) Internal engineering review (Skyline) — you confirm a time for our joint live demo and Q&A
2) Procurement packet review — I'll coordinate with Aditya to pull the quote and SLA exception language we discussed
3) Executive readout — 15–20 min slot for your CTO and VP of Data on Wednesday 9/15 if that works

If anything else is needed for procurement (certs, SOC 2 excerpts, sample contract language), flag it and I’ll loop in Sergio.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
O: +1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments: benchmark_raw.csv (CSV), map_reporting_kit_slide_deck.pdf (PDF), exec_readout_onepager.pdf (PDF), dashboard_snapshot.png (PNG)

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@skyline.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmark reporting kit and close checklist

Aisha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear materials. A couple of quick questions from my eng lead:
- Can you break out the p95 TTFT for the cold-start bucket vs warmed pool? The slide shows an aggregate number but our baseline cutoff is 200ms for p95 TTFT.
- On concurrency: the CSV has a spike at the 1,200 connection mark — do you have a run that shows steady-state behavior at 800–1000 connections (that's our expected production peak)?

Procurement will need the quote line items and any standard termination/SLA language you can share. Can Aditya send the draft?

We can do the exec readout on 9/15 at 11:00 PT — I'll confirm with CTO and send a calendar invite once I get procurement items.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Infrastructure | Skyline AI

Tom —

Attached is the finalized MAP reporting kit following our runs and yesterday's internal alignment. Highlights below and attachments included.

Highlights
- p95 TTFT (cold): 185ms at 800 connections, 210ms at 1,200 connections
- p95 TTFT (warmed pool): 95ms at 800 connections, 110ms at 1,200 connections
- Peak sustained throughput: 22k tokens/sec on A100-equivalent config during the 60s steady-state window
- Safety fallback: automatic routing to lower-capacity tuned variant when 99th percentile latency exceeds 300ms (included in slide notes)

- benchmark_raw.csv — includes the filtered 800–1000 run and added columns for cold/warm TTFT
- map_reporting_kit_slide_deck.pdf — updated with the split numbers and a one-slide risk/mitigation
